subject: MAP & Evaluation: POC environment readiness, canary activation and rollback playbook
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Alex Park <alex.park@novushealth.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: MAP kickoff — POC environment items (API keys / org setup / safelist / peering)

Alex, Patrick — thanks again for the time earlier. As promised, attaching a first-pass MAP spreadsheet that lays out the minimal path to get your POC into production-like conditions while keeping the window short for evaluation. High level ask for this note: please confirm owners and target dates for the items below so we can firm up the canary activation window.

Top-line commitments we need from Novus this week:
- Org seed and tenant creation (Novus-managed account + service account)
- API key exchange and ephemeral key policy for testing (we provide ephemeral key generator for canary)
- IP allowlist entries for Redwood host egress and health-check IPs (we've included a suggested CIDR range)
- VPC peering: routing CIDRs, security groups to allow port 443 + ephemeral management port 5500 for kernel health probes

Acceptance criteria for POC greenlight:
1) Test tenant created with 2 service accounts and at least one service principal for CI
2) Keys provisioned and validated against our sandbox (we'll run a signing test)
3) Peering established and a successful TCP health-check from our monitoring host
4) A canary test (10k tokens over 15mins) completes within agreed latency SLO and no auth errors

I've attached: MAP-Novus-v1.xlsx (timeline + owners), peering-config-template.yaml (example routes & SGs). Also included a short rollback playbook PDF that outlines immediate steps if we observe elevated error rates during canary.

Next step: can Novus confirm owners and a proposed 48-hour window between Dec 7-10 for canary activation? If those dates work, we'll schedule a brief preflight with Neha and Marissa to validate keys and peering.

Thanks —
Karthik
Karthik Iyer | Senior Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference
From: Alex Park <alex.park@novushealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Patrick Chan <patrick.chan@novushealth.com>, novus-ops@novushealth.com
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff — POC environment items (API keys / org setup / safelist / peering)

Karthik — thanks, this is helpful. Quick notes from our side:
- Owners: Patrick will own network & peering, I will own platform setup and API keys. Ops alias on copy for any firewall work.
- Dates: Dec 8-9 window looks better for us (we have a release freeze on Dec 7). Can we aim for a canary start on Dec 8 10:00 PT?
- Security ask: our infosec requires that ephemeral keys expire within 1 hour and that key-provisioning calls are logged to a SIEM. Is Redwood able to emit key activity to a syslog endpoint or provide an audit webhook?

Also we have a small constraint on allowed source IPs — our cloud NAT sits behind a handful of dynamic egress IPs. We'll supply the exact list by EOD today.

On rollback: the PDF is good. Two clarifying questions: what are the primary rollback triggers you recommend (error %, latency delta)? And are there steps to gracefully throttle the traffic back to hosted fallback model rather than full teardown?

—Alex
Alex Park | Head of Platform, Novus Health
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Alex Park <alex.park@novushealth.com>, Patrick Chan <patrick.chan@novushealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff — POC environment items (API keys / org setup / safelist / peering)

Alex — great, thanks for the quick owner assignment. Short answers to your asks:
- Ephemeral keys: yes — Redwood can issue ephemeral keys that expire at a configurable TTL. For the POC we'll set TTL=30m by default; we can change to 1h if that matches your policy. Each issuance is tracked and recorded in our audit stream. We can push audit events to a webhook URL (JSON payload) or to a syslog/forwarder via your collector.
- Rollback triggers (recommended):
  * Error rate > 5% sustained for 5 minutes (500/requests ratio)
  * Median latency increase > 2x baseline for 3 consecutive 1-minute buckets
  * Any auth failures affecting >1% of requests after key rotation
- Graceful degradation: we support a model fallback policy — if Canary fails, we can automatically route traffic to a pre-approved hosted variant (with a small cost delta) for up to 1 hour while infra issues are remediated. That avoids a hard teardown.

Action items for preflight (Neha/Marissa will validate):
1) Novus to share exact egress IP list (novus-ops) by EOD 12/2
2) Novus to create test tenant and two service accounts by 12/4
3) Redwood to share ephemeral key endpoint and test script by 12/4
4) Schedule 30m preflight call on Dec 7 08:30 PT (confirm or propose alternate)

If you confirm the Dec 8 10:00 PT canary, we'll lock the MAP timeline and circulate a runbook with precise bump/rollback commands.

Thanks —
Neha Kapoor
Engineering Lead, Customer Enablement
Redwood Inference
From: Alex Park <alex.park@novushealth.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Thanks Neha — confirmed on most items. Quick updates:
- Egress IPs: novus-ops will send the canonical list in the next hour.
- Tenant & service accounts: provisioning in progress; ETA 12/4 afternoon.
- Preflight call: Dec 7 08:30 PT works for Patrick and me. Please send calendar invite.
- Audit webhook: we prefer the webhook JSON option (send sample payload).

One last ask on the MAP spreadsheet: can you include a short column for rollback owner and expected downtime if rollback triggers? That will help our on-call routing.

I'll attach our IAM policy sketch separately (sent to your inbox).

—Alex
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Alex Park <alex.park@novushealth.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 07 Dec 2026 16:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff — POC environment items (API keys / org setup / safelist / peering)

Team — thanks for the confirmations and for routing the egress list. We're locked for the Dec 8 10:00 PT canary start. Final checklist before go:
- Novus: confirm attachment of peering-config-template.yaml to your networking ticket and ensure a route table update is queued with at least one rollback CIDR accepted.
- Novus: share webhook URL for audit events by 12/7 18:00 PT.
- Redwood: we'll deploy ephemeral key generator in your test tenant at 09:30 PT on Dec 8 and run a 10-min smoke test before the canary ramp.

Rollback & escalation plan (summary):
- Triage owner: Patrick Chan (Novus) for network; Marissa Cole (Redwood) for serving/runtime.
- Immediate action: pause canary ramp and switch traffic to hosted fallback (no tenant changes) 
- If elevated errors persist >15 minutes: initiate rollback playbook (POC-RollbackPlaybook.pdf) — remove peering (if network-related) and rotate test keys; estimated impact: up to 20 minutes plus any downstream cache invalidation.

I'll circulate a final runbook with step-by-step commands and the doc links to HubSpot this evening. Looking forward to a smooth run.

Regards,
Karthik
